annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "Night" on page 107 ("The Letter from the Midden"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. During this Age of Gods phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
Freud, Sigmund. The Interpretation of Dreams. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/4349
Troy, Mark L. Mummeries of Resurrection. http://www.rosenlake.net

annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Earwicker" on page 107 within "The Letter from the Midden": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of Biddy Doran the Hen scratching up the mysterious letter from the dump, the Book of Kells as model for textual exegesis. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie
